newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross mulls appeal for aid to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross mulls appeal for aid to N.Korea.

text.p: Red Cross officials have made fresh appeals to South Korea for food aid for North Korea but a recent submarine incursion by the communist nation has discouraged donations, Seoul Red Cross officials said on Saturday.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) this week asked South Korea to help raise 13.53 million Swiss francs ($10.65 million) for a fresh programme to stave off hunger for about 140,000 North Koreans hit by floods earlier this year, they said.
The federation said North Korea expected a shortfall of two million tonnes of grain next year, which represents about 40 percent of the Stalinist state's grain needs.
North Korea has faced the spectre of famine since July after floods destroyed an estimated 373,000 tonnes of grain, compounding damage from widespread flooding in 1995.
"We are considering the food aid appeal," said Seoul Red Cross spokesman Kim Hak-kyu. The new IFRC programme was to cover the period between December 1996 and October 1997.
"But it is difficult for us to secure donations because of anti-North Korean feelings prevalent since the intrusion of the North Korean submarine," another Seoul Red Cross official said.

The South Korean Red Cross had sent more than $1.7 million worth of relief goods, including blankets, flour, instant noodles and socks, to North Korea with funds raised through donations by South Koreans.
This is in addition to $3 million in aid given to North Korea by the Seoul government through the U.N. World Food Programme in an effort to ease child malnutrition.

Tensions have risen between North and South Korea since a North Korean submarine landed 26 agents on a South Korean beach in September. Twenty-four of them were shot dead, one was captured alive and another is still at large.
The Seoul government, calling the incursion a serious provocation, has suspend all assistance to North Korea and demanded Pyongyang apologise for the incident and guarantee no repeat.
Pyongyang insists the incident was an accident and demands the return of the bodies and the captured agent.
